stem: Which parts of the GRE General Test are section-level adaptive?
explanation: The two measures with two sections each, Verbal and Quantitative, are section-level adaptive.

choiceExplanations.A: Writing is a single task, not adaptive.

choices.text: Analytical Writing only
Verbal Reasoning and Quantitative Reasoning
Quantitative Reasoning only
Verbal Reasoning only
All five sections

stem: How difficult is the first Quantitative Reasoning section?
explanation: The first section of each measure is of average difficulty.

choiceExplanations.D: The first section is fixed at average difficulty.
choiceExplanations.E: The first section is fixed at average difficulty.

choices.text: Easy
Average difficulty
Hard
It depends on your Writing score
It depends on your Verbal score

stem: Dana answers nearly every question correctly in the first Quantitative section. What should she expect from the second Quantitative section?
explanation: Very strong performance on the first section leads to a second section at a higher level of difficulty.

choiceExplanations.B: Strong performance leads to a harder second section.
choiceExplanations.C: The second section is a different set.
choiceExplanations.D: Section order does not change this way.
choiceExplanations.E: Its difficulty depends on first-section performance.

choices.text: A higher level of difficulty
A lower level of difficulty
The same questions again
A Verbal section instead
No change in difficulty

stem: What does the difficulty of the second Verbal section depend on?
explanation: The second section's difficulty depends on overall performance on the first section of that measure.

choiceExplanations.C: Order of answering is not the basis.
choiceExplanations.D: Marking is a navigation tool, not the basis.

choices.text: Your overall performance on the first Verbal section
Your Analytical Writing task
The order in which you answered questions
The number of questions you marked
A random draw

stem: Which of the following statements about adaptation on the GRE General Test are true? Indicate all such statements.
explanation: Adaptation is at section level; scoring combines total correct across both sections with section difficulty.

choiceExplanations.B: Adaptation happens between sections, not question by question.
choiceExplanations.E: Only Verbal and Quant are adaptive.

choices.text: The first Verbal section is of average difficulty.
Each answer you give changes the difficulty of the very next question.
Scoring takes into account the total number of questions answered correctly across the two sections of a measure.
Scoring also takes into account the difficulty level of the sections.
Analytical Writing is section-level adaptive.

stem: A test-taker answers 9 of the 12 questions correctly in the first Verbal section and 11 of the 15 in the second. How many questions did she answer correctly across the two sections?
explanation: $9+11=20$. The total across the two sections is part of what scoring takes into account.

stem: Kim finds her second Quantitative section harder than her first and concludes that she must have done badly on the first. Is that conclusion justified?
explanation: A harder second section reflects a stronger first section, so feeling that it is hard is not a sign of failure.

choiceExplanations.A: It is the opposite: strong first-section performance leads to a harder second section.
choiceExplanations.C: Difficulty is set by first-section performance.

choices.text: Yes; a harder second section means a weak first section.
No; strong performance on the first section leads to a harder second section.
Yes; the second section is always harder.
No; the second section difficulty is random.
Yes; harder sections are only given to weak scorers.

stem: Which two things does scoring for Verbal and Quantitative combine?
explanation: Scoring uses the total correct across both sections and the difficulty of the sections.

choices.text: Only the number correct in the second section
The number correct across the two sections, and the difficulty level of the sections
Time spent per question, and number of marked questions
The Writing score and the first section's difficulty
Only the first section's difficulty

stem: A test-taker says: "The first Verbal section is of average difficulty anyway, so I will not try hard on it." Which response is best?
explanation: Both reasons to try hard hold: answers in the first section count, and your performance there determines the second section.

choiceExplanations.A: Answers in both sections count toward the score.
choiceExplanations.E: It depends on the first section.

choices.text: Right; only the second section counts.
Wrong: its answers count toward the total, and your performance on it sets the second section's difficulty.
Right; it is unscored.
Wrong: only Writing depends on it.
Right; the second section's difficulty is fixed in advance.

stem: Marcus answers 11 of 12 questions correctly in the first Quantitative section and 8 of 15 in the second. Priya answers 8 of 12 in the first and 11 of 15 in the second. Which statement is the most defensible?
explanation: Both have 19 correct, but Marcus's strong first section implies a harder second section. Since difficulty is part of scoring, equal totals do not guarantee equal scores.

choiceExplanations.C: Strong first-section performance, Marcus's, leads to the harder second section.
choiceExplanations.E: They count toward the total and set the second section.

choices.text: Their scores must be identical, since each answered 19 correctly.
Marcus probably faced the harder second section, and difficulty matters, so equal totals need not give equal scores.
Priya probably faced the harder second section.
Only second-section answers count, so Priya scores higher.
The first section's results are ignored.
